defects.claim: AppLixir 'has a signed server webhook: POST a signed HTTPS request to a publisher endpoint after server-side validation of each completed ad, MD5 signature from a shared secret, plus a Reward Management System that limits rewards per user within a dynamic 24-hour period and enforces a minimum time gap'; 'AppLixir is the only web vendor found offering a server-side completion signal' (finding marked verified; drives a 'must' recommendation and a 'later' recommendation).
defects.problem: The cited source (support.applixir.com/hc/en-us/articles/360053982873-Step-5-Setting-up-Web-Callback) returns HTTP 404, as does the un-slugged article ID. The AppLixir FAQ contains no occurrence of 'callback', 'webhook', 'server', 'signature' or 'Reward Management'. The support hub search for 'callback' surfaces only the client-side integration snippet `adStatusCallbackFn: (s) => s === 'ad-watched' && grantReward()`. No reachable AppLixir page substantiates a signed server-to-server callback or the RMS 24-hour/min-gap rules.
defects.correction: Downgrade to UNVERIFIED. Do not present AppLixir as having server-side completion verification unless AppLixir confirms it in writing or a live doc is found; the only documented reward path on AppLixir's public pages is a client-side status callback, i.e. spoofable like the Google web products.

defects.claim: 'since 14 Sep 2026 every gambling-and-games category (including social casino) needs certification' and numbers entry 'all gambling-and-games categories require certification from 14 Sep 2026; social casino applications move into Google Ads accounts from Sep 2026' (marked verified, citing support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/17258294 and seroundtable.com).
defects.problem: The cited Google page is titled 'Update to Gambling and Games Policy: Global (August 2026)', posted 23 Jul 2026, and every dated statement refers to 26 August 2026 ('On August 26, 2026, Google is updating its certification applications and standards...'; 'From August 26, all new applicants must use the revised forms'). It contains no 'September 14' and no statement that certification becomes newly required for all categories. The seroundtable URL in the brief is not in the sources list and the seroundtable page I could reach did not cover this.
defects.correction: Replace with: 'On 26 Aug 2026 Google revised its certification applications and standards for online gambling, non-casino games and social casino games; new applicants must use the new forms from that date.' Drop the 14 Sep 2026 date unless a primary source is found.

defects.claim: Google Play's Better Ads Experiences policy 'bans full-screen ads not closable after 15 seconds and interstitials before the app's loading screen, when you start a level or during the gameplay' (cited to answer/12271244); numbers entry 'must be closable within 15 seconds' sourced to the same page (marked verified).
defects.problem: answer/12271244 (Better Ads Experiences) contains no '15 seconds', 'closable/closeable' or 'loading screen' text. The verbatim rules ('Full screen interstitial ads of all formats that are not closeable after 15 seconds are not allowed'; 'Full screen video interstitial ads that appear before an app's loading screen (splash screen) are not allowed'; 'Ads that appear during game play at the beginning of a level or during the beginning of a content segment are not allowed') live in the Google Play Ads policy, answer/9857753.
defects.correction: Re-cite the 15-second and timing rules to support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9857753 (Ads policy). Keep the rewarded exemption quote, which is on 12271244.

defects.claim: Ad-blocker usage 'Germany near 49%' / 'about 49%' (headline risk, finding and numbers entry, sourced to backlinko.com, cropink.com, sqmagazine.co.uk citing GWI/Statista).
defects.problem: Backlinko's page (the only reachable one) gives Germany 31.5% of internet users aged 16-64; cropink.com/ad-blocker-statistics returns 404. The 49% figure appears nowhere reachable and is inconsistent with the GWI-based figure the brief otherwise relies on.
defects.correction: Use Germany ~31.5% (GWI via Backlinko) or state that sources range from ~31% to ~49% depending on methodology, with the 49% unverified.

defects.claim: 'suggested caps for casual games 6-10 rewarded views per session, 15-20 per day, with 60-120 s cooldowns (AppSamurai, 2025, unattributed)'; recommendation 'per-account caps (e.g. hard 15-20 per day, 60-120 s cooldown)'.
defects.problem: The cited AppSamurai post (dated 1 Jun 2026, not 2025) contains no frequency-cap figures at all: no per-session, per-day or cooldown numbers.
defects.correction: Remove the attribution; label the caps as the brief author's own design suggestion, or find a real source. Also correct the post date to June 2026.

defects.claim: coinis.com glossary: 'average of 2 views per DAU... healthy range 2-6'; 'Rewarded opt-in benchmark about 65%'; and coinis listed as a re-reporter of Tenjin Q4 2024 US eCPMs.
defects.problem: The coinis page gives a single studio case study with '2.1' views per DAU and a '64 percent' opt-in rate; there is no '2-6 healthy range' and no '65%' benchmark, and it contains no Tenjin Q4 2024 figures (its eCPM ranges are $15-40 tier-1, $3-10 tier-2/3 from AppLovin 2025).
defects.correction: Cite coinis as: one case study at 2.1 views/DAU and 64% opt-in; drop the '2-6 healthy range' and the '65%' as sourced; remove coinis from the Tenjin Q4 2024 source line (undrads.com alone carries those figures).

defects.claim: 'Unity data via Mistplay: users engaging with rewarded ads have 3.5x retention'; numbers entry 'Retention lift for rewarded-ad engagers: up to 3.5x'.
defects.problem: The Mistplay page attributes the 3.5x to games implementing offerwall campaigns ('retention rates up to 3.5x higher than industry averages'), not to rewarded-video engagers, and the fetched page does not attribute it to Unity.
defects.correction: Restate as 'offerwall campaigns: retention up to 3.5x industry average (Mistplay)'. Do not use as a rewarded-video retention lift.

defects.claim: Web rewarded CPM: 'AppLixir claims $8-15 CPMs'; numbers entry '$8-15 typical; $4-15 blended'; recommendation models 'web $8'.
defects.problem: AppLixir's FAQ does say '$8–15 CPMs', and its Aug 2026 benchmark post says blended '$4 to $15'. But AppLixir's own Sep 2026 post 'How much do rewarded video ads pay' states its live web inventory (100M+ impressions/month) averages '$4+ CPM', tier-1 '$7+', tier-3 '$1-2'. The vendor's most recent operating number is at the bottom of the quoted range, so '$8-15 typical' and an $8 web planning eCPM are optimistic.
defects.correction: Quote the range as '$4+ average, $7+ tier-1, $1-2 tier-3 (AppLixir Sep 2026); FAQ headline $8-15'. Use ~$4-7 as the web planning eCPM, not $8.

defects.claim: 'US rewarded eCPM, Android / iOS (Q2 2024) $30.25 / $24.39 — Tenjin x CAS benchmark via gamigion.com' (likely).
defects.problem: The gamigion report's eCPM data is from CAS.AI (Tenjin supplied only market-share data), and the per-country values exist only as chart images; the text cannot confirm $30.25/$24.39. The figures also sit far above Tenjin's Q4 2024 US iOS $19.63 / Android $16.49 and Mistplay's $15.15, which the brief presents alongside without noting the datasets are not comparable.
defects.correction: Attribute to CAS.AI, mark UNVERIFIED (chart-only), and note that cross-dataset ranges span ~$15-30 rather than implying a single US figure.

defects.claim: Playwire FAQ minimum '500,000 pageviews/month or 1,000 DAU for apps, majority US traffic'.
defects.problem: The FAQ gives the 500,000 pageviews / 1,000 DAU thresholds, but the geographic condition is 'a good footprint in English speaking countries (USA, UK, CA)', not 'majority US traffic'.
defects.correction: Replace 'majority US traffic' with 'a good footprint in English-speaking countries (USA, UK, CA)'.

defects.claim: H5 Games Ads evidence: adsense.google.com/start/h5-games-ads: 'It is a by-application product... Account approval is not guaranteed.' and 'Access requires an application, and approval is subject to partner eligibility' presented as quotes.
defects.problem: The adsense.google.com H5 page contains neither 'by-application' nor 'Account approval is not guaranteed'; it says 'Any publisher that owns an H5 games website is eligible to apply' and 'Google reserves the right to approve or disapprove the participation of any publisher'. The actual sentence 'Account approval is not guaranteed as it is subject to partner eligibility' is on support.google.com/adsense/answer/1705831. The other 'quote' is a paraphrase.
defects.correction: Cite 'Account approval is not guaranteed as it is subject to partner eligibility' and 'You need an approved AdSense account to show ads in your H5 games' to answer/1705831; drop the by-application 'quote' or mark it as paraphrase.

defects.claim: Rewards must be 'redeemable only within the publisher's platform' (presented in quotation marks in headline and finding).
defects.problem: The policy text is 'only redeemable and usable for an item or service within the publisher's platform, website or app'. The brief's quoted phrase is a paraphrase.
defects.correction: Quote the actual wording or remove the quotation marks. Substance is unaffected.

defects.claim: AdSense 'may only be implemented on web-based pages and approved WebView technologies' cited to support.google.com/adsense/answer/48182.
defects.problem: That sentence is not on answer/48182 (Program policies); it is in the Ad placement policies page, support.google.com/adsense/answer/1346295 ('Ads in a software application' section).

defects.claim: TopOn H1 2025: 'Android rewarded eCPM in midcore/hardcore games $6.70, described as a three-year low, -10% YoY' (verified).
defects.problem: The PDF says the midcore/hardcore Android rewarded eCPM of $6.7 is at 'multi-year lows, down 10% ... YoY'; the 'three-year lows' phrase is used for casual games (Android rewarded -7% YoY). The number and YoY are correct; the descriptor is transposed.
defects.correction: Say 'multi-year low, -10% YoY' for midcore/hardcore; 'near three-year lows, -7% YoY' applies to casual Android rewarded.

defects.claim: Google Play 'Since 28 Jan 2026 ... requires apps with real-money gambling/games/contests features to use Play age-screening tools' (finding marked verified, citing answer/9877032 plus a Lexology note).
defects.problem: The cited Google Play policy page contains no 28 Jan 2026 date and no mention of Play age-screening tools; only 'prevent under-age users from using the app'. The only support is a secondary law-firm note the brief itself calls secondary, yet the finding is graded 'verified'.
defects.correction: Downgrade this sub-claim to 'likely/secondary' or cite the Play policy-update announcement directly.

defects.claim: Ad Manager community thread 235861733 'confirms no SSV on web'; AdSense thread 180449812 supports the subdomain claim.
defects.problem: Both community threads render only navigation chrome via fetch; their content could not be read (the brief admits this for a different thread). They add no verifiable evidence.
defects.correction: Remove the threads as evidence; the Ad Manager help page (verbatim SSV sentence confirmed) and the Site Kit issue (parent-domain status confirmed) carry the claims on their own.

defects.claim: AppLovin MAX S2S callbacks 'HTTP GET with EVENT_ID and EVENT_TOKEN' (no algorithm stated) and AdMob SSV parameter list including user_id.
defects.problem: Minor: confirmed GET, 5 s timeout, 2 retries; EVENT_TOKEN is sha1(EVENT_ID + event key). AdMob SSV doc lists ad_network, ad_unit, custom_data, key_id, reward_amount, reward_item, signature, timestamp, transaction_id (user_id is optional and documented separately). No error, but the brief should not imply user_id is always present.
defects.correction: Note user_id/custom_data are only present when set in the SDK.

recomputed: 10,000 DAU x 2 rewarded/DAU = 20,000 impressions; x $15/1000 = $300/day (US). Correct.
20,000 impressions x $8/1000 = $160/day (web). Correct, but $8 is above AppLixir's latest stated web average ($4+); at $4 it is $80/day and at $7 (tier-1) $140/day.
AppLixir worked example: 4,000 impressions x $8/1000 = $32/day; $32 / 10,000 DAU = $0.0032 per DAU per day. Correct and matches the source.
DPDP Rules notified 13 Nov 2025 + 12 months = 13 Nov 2026 (consent managers); + 18 months = 13 May 2027. Consently's 13 May 2027 is the arithmetic result; Xident's 14 May 2027 is the off-by-one.
AdSense 80% of revenue after advertiser-platform fee: Google states 'about 68%' when the buyer is Google Ads; consistent with 80% x ~85% net. Matches source.
